summary: Streaming chat sessions disconnect or stall mid-generation (SSE/WebSocket) - intermittent latency/timeouts
description:
Issue summary: Multiple customers (first reported by NovaDocs) are seeing streaming chat sessions disconnect or stall mid-generation when responses exceed ~600 tokens.
Impact: Customer-visible truncation or stalled responses; repeated reconnects by clients; negative UX for chat product.
Environment: Production (us-east cluster), primarily affecting redwood-chat-v1 and an open quantized variant.
Steps to reproduce:
1) Start a streaming chat session (SSE or WebSocket) targeting redwood-chat-v1 in us-east.
2) Send a prompt that produces long-form output (>600 tokens) or uses multi-turn context.
3) Observe the stream: either the connection resets with a 502/504 at the client, or the stream remains open but stalls (no events) for >20s before reconnect attempt.
Observed behavior:
- Connection reset or 5xx returned by streaming-proxy for a subset (~7-12%) of long streams.
- Stalls: server stops emitting events; connection remains open; client-side heartbeats still show socket open; no new tokens for 15-45s then either resumed output or client reconnect.
Logs & metrics:
- Spikes in api-gateway downstream latency correlating with 5xx events.
- Serving runtime shows KV cache eviction and increased GPU busy-wait time on affected hosts.
- Streaming-proxy logs show repeated "upstream read timeout" for some connections.
- No obvious quota/rate-limit errors.
Temporary workaround: customer switched to non-streaming (polling) generation for long responses; this avoids mid-stream truncation but increases latency and cost.

investigation_notes: Collected proxy logs and request traces for provided request IDs. Upstream read timeout (streaming-proxy error) consistently appears ~40-60s into large responses for affected requests.

Api-gateway metrics show 95th percentile downstream latency increased from 120ms baseline to 1.8s during the incident window; correlated with GC and kernel scheduler load on a subset of serving hosts.

Runtime profiling indicates that quantized model variant has longer per-token kernel invocation times for sequences >512 which increases tail latency and causes apparent idle windows for the proxy's read loop.
Heap/KV cache churn: longer contexts cause eviction and rebuild cycles leading to brief stalls while KV refill happens. These stalls appear as silent periods on streaming channel.
No evidence of network flapping or client disconnects prior to stalls; TCP keepalive shows continuous connection. So likely server-side emission pause rather than network interruption.
Canary proxy timeout bump reduced outright truncations but did not eliminate stalls; suggests primary problem is runtime emission tail latency rather than strict proxy timeout threshold.
Related: SUP-24781 reports similar symptoms; linked for cross-reference. INT-4092 tracking infra changes.
Risk assessment: If unaddressed, enterprise customers producing longer outputs may see degraded UX; potential SLA impacts for chat flows with long answers.

Next steps: finish runtime low-risk change canary, monitor token emission rate metrics, add instrumentation for per-connection token latency to streaming-proxy logs, consider adaptive proxy timeouts or keepalive pings from runtime to proxy when emission pauses expected.
resolution: In progress. Temporary mitigations applied: increased proxy read-timeout to 90s for canary, customer offered routing to non-quantized model variant. Low-risk runtime KV-churn fix deployed to canary (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2241). Follow-up: monitor canary for 24-48h. If stable, schedule full rollout and then tighten proxy timeouts. Postmortem to be created if issue persists after full rollout.
